clue.text: Reade's ready

definitions.meaning: Charles Reade, the Victorian novelist, wrote a novel with this two-word title
the ready is slang for money in notes and coins, available at once

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the title of a Charles Reade novel; the other is slang for actual money, notes and coins rather than credit.

clue.text: Henry only caught one fish

indicators.note: caught says the words for Henry and only hold one inside them

parts.note: Hal is a pet name for Henry
but means only, as in 'but a child'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An angler called Henry landed just a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas, prized as food.

clue.text: NASA's business? Like its cost no doubt

definitions.meaning: the US space agency's work is launching spacecraft
costs that soar upwards very fast

explanation.definitionFit: Space launches are the agency's trade, and a soaring price climbs fast like a missile.

clue.text: She wrote 13 in French

parts.note: the clue 13 has the answer meaning beloved; in French that is the title of a famous novel by a woman writer

explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote Chéri, French for a beloved person.

clue.text: Like Raphael's Madonna not in this chapel

definitions.text: Like Raphael's Madonna not in this chapel

parts.words: Like Raphael's Madonna not in this chapel
parts.note: Raphael's painting named after the papal chapel hangs in Dresden, not in the chapel itself

explanation.definitionFit: The painting is named for Pope Sixtus, as is the Vatican chapel, yet it hangs in Dresden.

clue.text: A generally liked, if non-U, tree

indicators.note: non- here says the letter after it is to be left out of the word for generally liked

parts.note: something generally liked is popular
taken as written, the letter U

explanation.surface: A tree that most people like, if not quite upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is a real British phrase for not upper-class, which disguises the instruction to drop the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fast-growing tree of the willow family, common in lines along roads.

clue.text: Those manning Fleet Street? All but the last word

definitions.text: Those manning Fleet Street? All but the last word

parts.words: Those manning Fleet Street? All but the last word
parts.note: Fleet Street stands for the newspapers; drop the last word and those manning the fleet were the men who forced sailors to serve

explanation.definitionFit: Naval squads that forcibly recruited men for the fleet; the first word also names the newspapers of Fleet Street.

clue.text: Trouble after half a quart, duck?

indicators.note: after says the word for trouble comes behind the other piece

parts.note: a pint is half of a quart
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone drinks half a quart and is asked if they are feeling ill, love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a British term of endearment, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbling duck with a long pointed tail, found across the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: He saw Artemis bathing -- -at once a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster turns things upside down, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who glimpsed the goddess in her bath met calamity at once.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the hunter who saw Artemis bathing was turned into a stag and killed by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter of Greek myth who stumbled on the goddess bathing and was punished for it.

clue.text: Red resin, said before five years to become dull

indicators.note: said signals that the resin's name is heard, standing for a word spelt differently

parts.note: lac is a dark red resin made by insects
a lustre, or lustrum, is a period of five years

explanation.surface: Instructions for a resin that, after half a decade, loses its shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' makes the resin a homophone, and 'before' sets it ahead of the five-year period; 'to become' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacklustre lacks brightness and vitality, so it is flat and uninspiring.

clue.text: Mark or maybe pound

definitions.meaning: a mark, as in a written sign or a grade, is another word for the same thing
a pound was once a banknote, an example of paper money

explanation.definitionFit: A note is a mark or written sign, and the pound was a banknote, so 'maybe' signals an example.

clue.text: Pause for inspiration fatal for astronauts?

definitions.meaning: a short rest or respite from activity
inspiration in its literal sense of breathing in; doing that in outer space, a vacuum, would kill

explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a breather; read literally, the phrase is drawing breath in outer space, which would be deadly.

clue.text: Old warship made 1,000 retire in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder says the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient warship that forced a thousand men to fall back in a rout.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley of ancient Greece and Rome rowed with three banks of oars, used in naval battles.

clue.text: Facial growth must hurt? Nothing in it

indicators.note: in it says the zero goes inside the phrase must hurt

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: Does growing facial hair have to be painful? Not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a kind of facial hair.

clue.text: Wendy's Saving Grace

definitions.meaning: Wendy in Peter Pan has this surname
Grace of that surname was a lighthouse keeper's daughter who rescued shipwrecked sailors in 1838

explanation.definitionFit: Wendy's family name in Peter Pan, and the surname of the heroine who rowed out to save survivors of a wreck.

clue.text: Starts stirring one in its tea

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: stirring mixes these letters up like a spoon in a cup

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone begins stirring a single thing into a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin or set it going.

clue.text: Infrequent visitor takes us in devotional exercise

indicators.note: takes says the first piece adds the next one after it

parts.note: angels' visits are proverbially few and far between
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who rarely calls brings us along to prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic prayer recited morning, noon and evening, marked by the ringing of a bell.

clue.text: Disgusting row is out of order

indicators.note: is out of says the word for row sits outside the order abbreviation

parts.note: a row is a noise or din
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A rowdy argument is described as nasty and against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' looks like an anagram signal; it is 'is out of' (contains) plus order, OM (the Order of Merit, a British honour).
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling, nothing to do with noise.

clue.text: Planting a pole on top of it would be extremely hard

definitions.text: Planting a pole on top of it would be extremely hard

parts.words: Planting a pole on top of it would be extremely hard
parts.note: climbers plant a flag pole on the world's highest summit; put the letter for a compass pole on top and the word says one could never relax

explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain on Earth, where climbing to plant a flag is famously hard.

clue.text: One man's meat for such a one otherwise his gore?

definitions.text: One man's meat for such a one

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters are arranged in another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man-eater might say one man's meat is another's poison, while blood runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'one man's meat is another man's poison': for a man-eating monster, a man is the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a man-eating giant of fairy tales, for whom a human is simply a meal.

clue.text: No lines in fruit

parts.note: O is zero, none
ranges are lines or rows, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Fruit that comes with no lines at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruits are examples of the general class fruit.

clue.text: The following being always about one up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole is read from bottom to top
about says the word for always goes round the word for one

parts.note: e'er is a poetic shortening of ever, always
a unit is one

explanation.surface: A follower is always on hand for someone superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Stableman could lose his head yet keep his job

definitions.text: Stableman could lose his head yet keep his job

parts.words: Stableman could lose his head yet keep his job
parts.note: drop the first letter of this word for a groom and what remains is another word for the same job

explanation.definitionFit: A groom at an inn who tends horses, also spelt without its first letter.

clue.text: Issue of a Syracusan merchant comically and erroneously confused

definitions.text: Issue of a Syracusan merchant comically and erroneously confused

parts.words: Issue of a Syracusan merchant comically and erroneously confused
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors the merchant Egeon of Syracuse has two sons so alike that everyone mixes them up

explanation.definitionFit: The two Antipholus brothers are offspring of one birth who look exactly alike, the source of the farce.

clue.text: A great book in my view

definitions.meaning: as it seems ..., two words run together

explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big weighty volume, and split in two it is the phrase for 'as I see it'.

clue.text: Study Latin, for example, the wrong way? What idiots!

parts.note: to con is to study or learn

indicators.note: the wrong way says the words for Latin and for example are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that studying Latin backwards is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Old phrasing spoke of people with an inborn mental deficiency as congenital idiots: present from birth.

clue.text: Mallet to crush an insect

definitions.meaning: a heavy wooden mallet for ramming or pounding

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a heavy wooden pounding tool and a hard-shelled insect.

clue.text: Judge's assistant in return trip crosses safely

indicators.note: return trip says the run is read going back the way it came
in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A court official on a journey home gets safely across.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal adviser who sits with a judge or magistrate on technical matters.
